scenario: User pastes an abstract about a new measurement of neutrino oscillation parameters using a novel detector array, no other context given.
expected_behavior: build manuscript profile before suggesting any journal
classify contribution_type as measurement (primary) with possible method as secondary
classify article_type as original research / letter, not assumed without checking length cues
leave word_count, reference_count, current_stage as unknown since not provided
do not invent audience beyond disciplinary specialists without evidence
notes: Tests baseline manuscript-first discipline and unknown-field honesty.

scenario: User says: 'I wrote a paper arguing against a specific interpretation of Kant's categorical imperative, engaging closely with three recent commentators.'
expected_behavior: classify contribution_type as conceptual distinction and/or normative argument
classify article_type as philosophical article
classify method fit as low relevance per humanities weighting
identify audience as disciplinary specialists (Kant scholars) not general philosophers without more info
flag technical_depth and word_count as unknown
notes: Tests humanities-specific profiling and correct low weighting of quantitative method fit.

scenario: User provides a structured abstract of a multi-site RCT testing a new anticoagulant vs standard of care, n=1200, primary endpoint stroke incidence.
expected_behavior: classify research_design as RCT
classify contribution_type as clinical evidence (primary), causal evidence (secondary)
flag CONSORT relevance as an adaptation/compliance consideration, not force other unrelated guidelines
classify clinical_relevance as high
classify article_type as clinical study / original article
notes: Tests correct reporting-guideline mapping without over-forcing irrelevant checklists (e.g. should not suggest PRISMA).

scenario: User shares a 12-page paper proving a new bound on a class of combinatorial optimization problems, includes formal proofs, no applied results.
expected_behavior: classify contribution_type as theorem/method contribution, not empirical finding
classify technical_depth as high
de-emphasize writing-architecture/audience concerns relative to subject classification and problem-class per mathematics.md
leave geographic_scope and temporal_scope as not applicable / unknown rather than forcing a value
notes: Tests that irrelevant fields are marked unknown/not-applicable rather than fabricated.

scenario: User describes a manuscript offering a doctrinal reinterpretation of a specific line of comparative constitutional cases across three jurisdictions, no empirical data.
expected_behavior: classify contribution_type as doctrinal reinterpretation with comparative evidence as secondary
classify article_type as legal doctrinal paper, not empirical article
identify audience as legal scholars
note jurisdictional/comparative scope as a first-order profile field per law.md
notes: Tests law-specific genre classification and avoidance of forcing empirical-legal-studies framing onto doctrinal work.

scenario: User pastes a paper introducing a new benchmark dataset for evaluating LLM reasoning, with baseline model comparisons.
expected_behavior: classify contribution_type as dataset/benchmark (primary), with method/algorithm possibly secondary
flag that in this subfield a conference-first strategy may be more appropriate per engineering-computing.md, without assuming it forces conference-only
classify audience as technical engineers / methodologists
leave temporal_scope/geographic_scope as not applicable rather than invented
notes: Tests correct contribution classification and awareness of venue-type norms in fast-moving CS subfields.

scenario: User provides an abstract using a difference-in-differences design on administrative tax data from one country to estimate a labor-market policy effect.
expected_behavior: classify research_design/methods as DiD, data as administrative
classify contribution_type as causal evidence
classify geographic_scope as single-country and flag portability/generalizability as a distinct dimension to address later, not as an automatic penalty
classify policy_relevance as medium-high given policy-effect framing
notes: Tests correct handling of single-country causal studies without premature regional penalty.

scenario: User: 'My paper compares bureaucratic discretion across three Nordic countries using interview data with senior civil servants.'
expected_behavior: classify methods as qualitative/interview-based, research_design as comparative study
classify contribution_type as comparative evidence
classify unit_of_analysis as institutional/bureaucratic actors
classify geographic_scope as multi-country regional (Nordic) rather than 'international' without justification
notes: Tests precision in geographic_scope field rather than defaulting to vague categories.

scenario: User shares a preregistered experiment (n=340) testing a cognitive-bias intervention, includes a power analysis and OSF link.
expected_behavior: classify research_design as experimental article
note current_stage may reflect preregistration status if stated, otherwise unknown
classify contribution_type as causal evidence / mechanism
recognize preregistration as relevant to open-science requirements for later hard-filter consideration, not as a manuscript profile field that gets invented if unstated elsewhere
notes: Tests linkage between manuscript profile and downstream open-science hard-filter awareness.

scenario: User: 'My paper argues, on normative grounds, that current AI governance frameworks misapply the precautionary principle. No empirical data, no policy case study.'
expected_behavior: classify contribution_type as normative argument, not policy analysis or empirical finding
classify article_type as philosophical article / conceptual paper, not empirical policy study
flag explicitly that a topically-relevant 'AI governance' journal may still be a method/genre mismatch if it mainly publishes empirical policy work, per fit-model.md Research-design fit
classify interdisciplinarity as genuinely-cross-cutting but identify home discipline as philosophy/normative theory
notes: Direct test of the canonical topic-vs-method-vs-genre mismatch example from the spec.
